# Issue #869: Measure the remaining method gaps after the positive-control thread closed and scope the XML key confirmation

## Goal
The positive-control thread (#763 f4) is closed: review #866 was CLEAR on the last pin correction (#865). Now measure what is left. Report, do not fix. Write `benchmark/challenges/next-gap-0202.md`. Change no other repository file.

Part 1, gaps: for each remaining readiness gap in `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`, give its status (OPEN / PARTIAL / CLOSED) and cite the evaluation.md line plus at least one repository file:line as evidence. Cover at least the challenges row (evaluation.md near line 69), dependency/native keys, restricted split/allocation/isolation, reader/probes/scorer integration, and independent whole-method review with owner acceptance.

Part 2, XML key confirmation: find out whether `benchmark/challenges/positive-control-key-0191.json` already has an independent confirmation of its XML literals against the fixture XML. The cold derivation was 0191 and the literal/locator/hash check was #828 F1. If it does, say so with evidence. If it does not, write the exact missing check: inputs, who must not have seen the key, and the expected output.

Part 3, recommendation: name one next task. It must not need LabVIEW, owner material or product code. Give its expected gain and a verification command that can be written.

Expected gain: the next shaper reads `## Recommendation` and orders it without surveying again.

TOOLS, read first: your tools are JSON actions that the parent broker runs. You may see "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session". That is the model CLI refusing a NATIVE tool call; the broker tools still work. Propose the same operation again as a JSON action. Never stop or report blocked because of it. Grep matches one literal substring only: no `(`, `|` or `\b`.

No session can run LabVIEW. Make no claim about LabVIEW behaviour.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.session/exports/manifest.json` checked; the #866 report verdict is noted.
- [ ] `benchmark/challenges/next-gap-0202.md` has the headings `## Gaps`, `## XML key confirmation` and `## Recommendation`.
- [ ] Every gap row in `## Gaps` has a status and an evaluation.md line reference.
- [ ] `## XML key confirmation` states either covered (with evidence) or the exact missing check.
- [ ] `## Recommendation` names one task with its expected gain and a verification command.
- [ ] `git status --porcelain` lists only the new file and no `__pycache__`. Do not commit.

## Verification
python3 -B -c "t=open('benchmark/challenges/next-gap-0202.md').read(); assert all(h in t.splitlines() for h in ('## Gaps','## XML key confirmation','## Recommendation')); print('next-gap-0202 headings: OK')"

## Context
- Closed, do not redo: #820 gap measurement, 0191 cold key, #828 F1/F3, #831 F2, #856/#857 controls, #860/#861/#865/#866 pins. gap-0160 and scorer-probe-0164: do not survey again; cite them.
- Carried limits: #831 (the scorer never checks citations against the XML artifact); #809 f2 and f4; #763 f6; plan-0189 does not count vi-actor-core-native-gap.json.
- If you import benchmark/scripts/*.py, use `python3 -B` and check `git status --porcelain` (#785).

## Budget
Read: `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md` whole (it is in Polish); `benchmark/challenges/positive-control-plan-0189.md`; `benchmark/challenges/README.md`; the #866 report. For `benchmark/challenges/positive-control-key-0191.json` and `benchmark/challenges/library-specialty.json`, read their top-level keys and the ranges you cite only. Do not read `benchmark/results/**`, `journal/**` or history records. Short command output only. Write the file early and refine it.

# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and
assertion-critique method; provenance is in `docs/perpetua/roles.md`.
It follows `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; read that contract and
`goal/goal.md` before designing cases. Protocol and report: the engine contract in your system instructions.
A separate reviewer session checks preparation evidence and the method. The evaluator verifier checks evaluator changes only; it does not replace method review or owner acceptance.
The report starts with `<!-- session-report -->`, then a fenced `yaml` block with `status: wip` while you work.
Finish takes the same one word as that status: `done`, `partial`, `blocked` or `rejected` (#584 lost two Finish
calls: status `complete`, then a report without the marker).

Write only `benchmark/`: protocol, provenance and coverage records, development cases,
repeatable preparation scripts and the optional preparation evidence index. Keep large
originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

`benchmark/preparation.json` pins a SHA256 for each evidence file. When assigned work changes
an indexed file or adds milestone evidence, update the corresponding hashes in the same change.
Each evidence file must stay under 2 MB. Run `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`
for indexed changes only when the task permits that command. If the task forbids evaluator
checks, report that restriction and run only its permitted verification. Never add an evaluator
invocation as extra verification of an unindexed preparation package (#643). An index check
establishes file integrity, not method readiness or product quality. The engine imports final
file bytes; no agent commit is required.

For the assigned part of the protocol:

1. State the question, expected observable behavior and verifiable location in the original
   artifact. Establish expected answers independently of the reader being tested. Record
   the method, evidence and uncertainties; unavailable native evidence stays unavailable.
2. Account for artifact families, versions, dependencies and inaccessible diagrams. Keep
   unsupported or unexecuted cases visible. The first corpus does not redefine the goal.
3. Specify project/family splits, duplicate checks and how evaluation cases and answer keys
   will be withheld from the evaluated agent. The repository and its history are public:
   do not commit withheld cases or keys here, including under `policy/evaluator/`.
   Design an access boundary and request missing capability before claiming isolation.
4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,
   uncertainty and separate reading-fidelity, answer-correctness and source-grounding checks.
5. Exercise the method with wrong answers, wrong source locations, a constant exporter and
   an unsupported case. Link executed evidence and explicit failures. Independently derived
   expectations must distinguish correct and deliberately wrong outputs.

Inspect actual outputs, rather than relying on the execution report. For each expectation,
cite evidence of the substantive result; correct filenames and valid hashes alone do not
pass. Extract and verify implicit factual, process and quality claims. Flag unverifiable
claims and assertions that would also pass a clearly wrong output, or important outcomes
that no assertion checks. These checks adapt the grader instructions; they do not grant
this author independent approval of their own method.

Completion means the assigned evidence is reproducible, not that the benchmark is ready.
Report which prerequisites remain missing. Request a separate reviewer session for the
preparation evidence and a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change when executable scoring is
needed. Only the evaluator role changes `policy/evaluator/`; its independent verifier must
pass before that change takes effect. Product implementation waits for independent method
review and owner acceptance of the pinned protocol and evidence. Numeric thresholds,
scope changes and the goal gate remain owner decisions.

## Role tools (Policymaker #854)

Your tools are JSON actions that the parent broker runs. The model CLI itself has no native tools.
If you call a native tool, the CLI answers "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session".
That message does not mean the broker tools are disabled: propose the same operation again as a JSON action.
Never stop or report `blocked` because of this message. #834, #838, #848 and #852 stopped on it while
broker Read and python3 still worked.

Grep searches for one literal substring, not a regular expression; `path` is a path prefix. A pattern with
`(`, `|` or `\b` finds nothing (#848, #852). Use one literal pattern per Grep call.

# Public development challenge inputs

Generated by `python3 -I benchmark/scripts/challenges.py`; verify with `python3 -I benchmark/scripts/challenges.py --check`.
No environment variable, prepared source cache or non-stdlib package is needed. `--check` regenerates in memory, never writes, and rejects differing, missing or extra entries (including README and nested files).

These are synthetic inputs and authored expectations, not executed challenges or scorer results. Three public cases are planned; zero reader attempts, executions or scores exist. Every probe preserves its exact synthetic request/response text, UTF-8 SHA256, simulated failure/truncation record, and per-ID alignment. Null timestamps/revisions mean no execution evidence exists. The concrete reader adapter is unavailable.

Both libraries freeze 12 IDs per dimension: ten XML declaration IDs plus two unavailable native IDs. The VI freezes three native IDs per dimension. Every positive submission includes all IDs; unavailable answers are null, carry no fabricated citation, and remain unverified. All ten XML literals have their real supporting inventory locators. No complete positive control can currently earn `correct`: native-required slots prevent it. `expected.per_id` is the provisional author's XML expectation conditional on independent confirmation; `current_evidence_per_id` additionally marks XML matches unverified pending that review. Dimensions and all seven outcome counts are recorded for both fixed inventories; extra outcomes are separate and never alter denominators. Reader matches are always unverified without native references. Known XML contradictions are deliberately incorrect author expectations, pending independent confirmation of the underlying evidence.

The table covers every [protocol challenge row](../protocol.md#challenges). Control names below occur in [library-icon-tests.json](library-icon-tests.json) unless another fixture is named. [library-specialty.json](library-specialty.json) supplies the second positive and constant-export comparison; [vi-actor-core-native-gap.json](vi-actor-core-native-gap.json) supplies unsupported conditions.

| Protocol row | Fixture/control names | Setup or explicit gap, and why |
|---|---|---|
| Positive controls | Both libraries: `positive-control` | Full materialized submissions and ten supporting XML locators; two native answer slots null. Whole correctness/grounding and fidelity are unverified. Independent XML checking and native evidence are gaps; no scorer that rejects everything has been validated. |
| Wrong answer | `wrong-answer-declared-dependency` | Replace A0007's literal declared member URL, retain its valid source locator, and preserve original/replacement evidence. Correctness and grounding incorrect. This tests a dependency declaration literal; computation, runtime dependencies and typedef-impact challenges are explicit gaps requiring controlled native evidence. |
| Wrong citation | `wrong-citation-existing`, `wrong-citation-unresolvable` | Correct A0005 uses real A0008 location (different member name), or syntactically valid `/Library/Item[999999]/@Name`. A0005 grounding incorrect independently of matching answer content. |
| Selective omission | `selective-omission-answer`, `selective-omission-reader`, `true-extra-with-omission-answer`, `true-extra-with-omission-reader` | A0008/R0008 stays missing among 12 required slots; extra true content cannot replace it. Overall assessments remain unverified because native references are unavailable. The protocol's fully checked partial-case demonstration is an explicit gap; a conditional XML-only answer tally would be 9 correct/1 missing, with 2 native slots separately unverified. |
| Extra false claim | `extra-false-answer`, `extra-false-reader`, `extra-true-answer`, `extra-true-reader`, `extra-unverified-answer`, `extra-unverified-reader` | Concrete extra UTF-8 literal-length assertions are falsified/supported by A0005 and a recorded byte-length derivation. False answer uses existing non-supporting A0001 citation. Native member-count assertion is explicitly unverified. False extras make the affected authored dimension incorrect; true reader extras remain unverified without native alignment. |
| Duplicate and contradiction | `duplicate-answer`, `duplicate-reader`, `contradiction-answer`, `contradiction-reader` | Preserve two equivalent assertions or assertion plus explicit negation, with both raw pointers and evidence. Duplicate counted once; contradiction makes A0005/R0005 and its dimension incorrect. |
| Constant export | Both libraries: `constant-export` | Identical fixed bytes assert R0001=20008000 and R0005=Actor.lvclass. R0005 contradicts Test Caller.vi and Batch Msg.lvclass respectively; R0001 also contradicts icon-tests 21008000. Remaining ten observations stay missing; fidelity authored expectation incorrect in both. Native comparisons are an explicit gap. |
| Empty, truncated or failed probe | `empty-probe`, `wrapper-only-probe`, `truncated-probe`, `unsupported-probe`, `failed-probe` | Preserve empty bytes, valid wrapper without observations, exact incomplete JSON prefix, explicit missing-runtime response, and concrete error JSON/exit 1 respectively. All required fidelity slots missing, unsupported or error as appropriate. Calls and failures are simulated fixture inputs. |
| Unsupported or inaccessible case | VI: `unsupported-missing-runtime`, `unsupported-missing-dependency`, `unsupported-missing-license`, `unsupported-inaccessible-diagram` | Concrete abstentions and exact injected conditions retain all three IDs, unsupported outcomes, and planned=1/attempted=executed=scored=0 per control. These are controlled declarations, not observed environment failures or demonstrated behavior. |
| Missing evidence or execution | `missing-independent-key`, `missing-native-run`, `zero-executed-tests` | Materialized null-key/native-run and zero-test report records. All remain unverified/unexecuted; no key is inferred from synthetic responses. |
| Diagram difference (paired revisions) | none: explicit gap | No diagram-difference (paired-revision) control exists. Missing evidence: before/after revisions of the same VI, native diagram evidence for both, and an independently established difference key. This remains a visible gap and the case stays in scope. |

Every control carries full submitted records, exact raw text, fixed per-ID ledgers, outcome counts, separate extras/duplicate/contradiction ledgers and evidence pointers. Null native slots are not factual assertions. Structural XML inspection makes no hardware, execution, resolved-membership, effective-scope or compatibility claim. Native locators cannot be supplied from these inventories, and remain explicit gaps.

Next: independently check all provisional XML expectations and original locators, review the accounting and synthetic raw alignments, then request a Policymaker-ordered scorer with separate evaluator verification. Native references, a concrete adapter and actual substantive comparisons remain required. Public inputs are unsuitable as withheld evaluation evidence; no readiness, threshold, scope or LabVIEW 2024 claim is made.

# Ocena początkowa i droga do benchmarku

Stan startowy: **skuteczność narzędzia niezmierzona, benchmark nie istnieje**.
Temat setupu przygotowuje ocenę; nie buduje produktu ani docelowego zestawu przypadków.
Podstawą są ustalenia [niezależnej weryfikacji](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/10#issuecomment-6225343449)
i [dostępu do środowiska](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/2#issuecomment-6248028771).
Kompilacja przykładu VI z 2014 w kontenerze NI 2026 Q1 dowodzi dostępu do tego środowiska,
nie poprawności czytnika, VI Scripting ani obsługi wszystkich wersji. Dostęp 2024 pozostaje niezweryfikowany.

## Co rozstrzyga skrypt, a co właściciel

Zachowano dostarczoną bramkę `gate.kind: owner`. Każda zmiana pracy czeka na decyzję
właściciela; nie zaakceptowano progów jakości ani samodzielnego kończenia celu.
Właściciel ocenia treść dowodów, dopuszcza rozpoczęcie implementacji dopiero po wiarygodnej
metodzie weryfikacji, akceptuje progi sukcesu i ewentualną zmianę zakresu. W temacie D
zaakceptował zasady sukcesu zapisane w `goal/goal.md`: pełny zakres, osobne pomiary
wierności odczytu i odpowiedzi popartych źródłem oraz niezależny benchmark z porównaniem.
Progi jakości i wykonywalna bramka celu czekają na wiarygodny benchmark i osobną
akceptację właściciela; przyszła bramka wymaga `owner_confirms: true`. Plik
`goal/gate.yml` pozostaje nieobecny, więc pętla nie ogłasza samodzielnie sukcesu. Zastąpienie
bramki skryptem wymaga jego decyzji oraz niezależnie sprawdzonej metody. Nie jest to
ograniczenie celu do wersji lub rodzin obecnych w pierwszych przykładach.

`check` uruchamia `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` w kandydacie. Sprawdza
jedynie poprawność opcjonalnego indeksu dowodów: schemat, lokalne ścieżki, niepuste pliki
i SHA256. Brak indeksu jest normalnym stanem początkowym, raportowanym jawnie; błędny
istniejący indeks zatrzymuje zmianę. Ten check nie potwierdza treści dokumentów ani jakości.
Nie wykonuje kodu wskazanego w dowodach. Testy tego skryptu i silnika nie są benchmarkiem LabVIEW.

Raport porównawczy uruchamia się z **zaakceptowanego drzewa**, podając oba katalogi:

```sh
python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --baseline /accepted --candidate /candidate
```

Obsługiwane są też `BASELINE_DIR` i `CANDIDATE_DIR`. Ostatnia linia to JSON zgodny z
kontraktem silnika. Raport zawiera oba stany; błędne dowody kandydata dają `rejected`,
pozostałe przypadki `inconclusive`, zawsze `improved: false`. Nawet komplet odnośników
nie oznacza gotowości benchmarku. `tool_quality: null`, `benchmark_executed: false` oraz
`benchmark_ready: false` pozostają jawne. Raport jest pomocą dla właściciela; przy bramce
`owner` silnik nie uruchamia go automatycznie i nie wykorzystuje go do automatycznego przyjęcia.
Brak pomiaru pozostaje brakiem pomiaru, także po usunięciu lub wymianie indeksu.

Indeks `benchmark/preparation.json` powstanie podczas pracy pętli. Wzór, nie gotowy benchmark:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"milestones":{"sources":[],"tasks":[],"oracle":[],"split":[],"coverage":[],"baseline":[],"challenges":[]}}
```

Każda lista zawiera wpisy `{"path":"benchmark/protocol.md","sha256":"<64 znaki SHA256>"}`.
Dowody muszą być plikami w drzewie, bez symlinków, do 2 MB każdy; duże dane opisuje mały
rekord z przypiętym źródłem i hashem. Sekcje i liczba odnośników służą nawigacji, nie punktacji.
Check działa tylko dla zmian pracy; ścieżki polityki/audytu/dziennika omijają go zgodnie
z silnikiem. Weryfikator sam uruchamia testy każdej zmiany evaluatora.

## Co musi powstać przed implementacją

Pętla przygotuje następujące dowody, następnie niezależny weryfikator sprawdzi metodę,
a właściciel oceni jej wiarygodność przed przyjęciem implementacji. Nie wystarczy utworzyć pliki.

| Obszar | Wymagane ustalenia i dowody |
|---|---|
| sources | Pochodzenie, licencja, commit i SHA256 oryginałów; zależności, wersja zapisu artefaktu i wersja środowiska odczytu osobno. Zachować oryginał przed konwersją. |
| tasks | Zadania o przepływie danych, typach, strukturach, zależnościach, projektach i znaczeniu zmian; ocenialna odpowiedź i wskazanie źródła w oryginale. |
| oracle | Odpowiedzi ustalone niezależnie od czytnika: diagramy i właściwości w LabVIEW, kontrolowane wejścia/wyjścia, dokumentacja, raporty różnic i zapis niezależnej kontroli. Sam eksport badanego narzędzia nie jest wzorcem. |
| split | Rozdział rozwoju i oceny według całych projektów i rodzin; wykrywanie kopii/wariantów. Nowe własne przypadki ograniczają ryzyko znajomości publicznych przykładów przez model. Klucz i część oceniająca poza dostępem badanego agenta; w publicznym repo nie da się ukryć ich samą ścieżką. Przed pomiarem sprawdzić faktyczną izolację. |
| coverage | Inwentaryzacja wszystkich rodzin, wersji, modułów i warunków dostępu; pokrycie jawne, bez usuwania trudnych przypadków z mianownika. Pierwszy zestaw nie redefiniuje celu. |
| baseline | Powtarzalne porównanie tych samych zadań bez narzędzia, z obrazami gdy dostępne, oraz z narzędziem; ten sam model, prompt i budżet, przypięte wersje, powtórzenia, koszt i czas. |
| challenges | Próby metody na celowo błędnych odpowiedziach, błędnych wskazaniach źródła, stałym/pustym eksporcie i nieobsługiwanym przypadku. Zero wykonanych testów, brak runtime lub klucza nie dają zaliczenia. |

Początkowa inwentaryzacja obejmuje VI (panel i diagram), kontrolki i typedefy, biblioteki,
klasy, projekty i build specs, testy, zasoby, zależności, pakiety, skompilowane dystrybucje
oraz warianty modułów i targetów; lista pozostaje otwarta. Wyniki mają osobne przekroje
według rodziny, wersji zapisu i środowiska. Nieprzebadana wersja ma brak pokrycia.
Wariant 2024 wolno wybrać dopiero po przedstawieniu dodatkowego nakładu dla wszystkich
wersji i ograniczeń zgodności, zgodnie z celem; ten setup nie wybiera wariantu zapasowego.

Przyszły raport oddzieli wierność odczytu od poprawności odpowiedzi agentów i ich poparcia
w źródle. Wskaże liczbę zaplanowanych i rzeczywiście wykonanych przypadków oraz wyniki
poprawne, częściowe, nieobsługiwane, brak zależności/licencji/środowiska, chroniony/usunięty
diagram i błąd narzędzia. Uczciwe zgłoszenie ograniczenia nie dowodzi pełnego odczytu.
Sprawdzenie struktury bez sprzętu nie potwierdza zachowania na sprzęcie. Tolerancje,
niedeterminizm i przedziały niepewności trzeba określić przed porównaniem. Nie agregować
tych wymiarów do arbitralnego jednego wyniku ani nie przyjmować progu sukcesu bez właściciela.

## Niezależna kontrola zmian

Evaluator zmienia tylko uprawniona rola, na zlecenie Policymakera. Silnik wymaga odrębnej
sesji weryfikatora i przypina jej zgodę do commita i drzewa evaluatora. Stara wersja
obowiązuje do wyniku `pass`; zmieniony snapshot wymaga ponownej kontroli.
Instrukcje weryfikatora, wspólny kontrakt roli i protokół są chronione w `engine.yml`.
Silnik blokuje też zmianę/usunięcie wpisu `evaluator-verifier` w profilach, zachowując
możliwość tworzenia pozostałych ról. Zmiana tych zabezpieczeń należy do właściciela.
Niezależność oznacza osobną sesję i dowody, nie gwarancję bezbłędności modelu; przy
niepewności weryfikator odmawia `pass`. To nie bramka końcowego sukcesu; jej odroczenie
i wymagane potwierdzenie właściciela zapisano w `goal/goal.md` w temacie D.

# Positive-control plan (issue #820, #763 finding 4)

Plan only. No control, fixture, score.py or results file was changed. No LabVIEW behaviour is claimed.
Benchmark readiness stays false.

## Gap

Command (run with `python3 -B -I`, reads fixture bytes only, no score.py import):

```
python3 -B -I -c "import json,glob,sys
sys.dont_write_bytecode=True
for f in sorted(glob.glob('benchmark/challenges/library-*.json')):
    c=json.load(open(f,encoding='utf-8'))['controls']
    ok=lambda e:sum(v=='correct' for d in('correctness','grounding') for v in e['per_id'][d].values())
    dim=sum(1 for x in c if 'correct' in (x['expected']['dimensions']['correctness'],x['expected']['dimensions']['grounding']))
    print(f,'controls',len(c),'dim_correct',dim,'per_id_correct_expected',sum(ok(x['expected']) for x in c),'with_expected_positive',sum('expected_positive' in x for x in c),'positive_per_id_correct',sum(ok(x['expected_positive']) for x in c if 'expected_positive' in x))"
```

Output:

```
library-icon-tests.json controls 28 dim_correct 0 per_id_correct_expected 0 with_expected_positive 1 positive_per_id_correct 20
library-specialty.json controls 3 dim_correct 0 per_id_correct_expected 0 with_expected_positive 1 positive_per_id_correct 20
```

Reading: 31 controls in library-*.json (28 + 3). The 35 in results/challenges.json also include the 4 controls of vi-actor-core-native-gap.json, which this script does not count.
Kinds present: positive-control (2, both expect `unverified` on every dimension), wrong answer/citation (4), extras/omission/duplicate/contradiction
(icon-tests only), probe-failure shapes (empty, wrapper-only, truncated, unsupported, failed), absence-of-evidence (3), constant exports (constant-export and constant-keyed-literal-export, in both files).
**0 of 31 controls expect a `correct` correctness or grounding outcome in `expected`.** The only `correct` outcomes appear in the `expected_positive` block of the two positive-control entries (20 per-id outcomes each: 10 correctness + 10 grounding). `regression_self_test` consumes them only with synthetic execution counters (executed=1, scored=1). Those blocks are authored in the same fixture and role family as the scorer, and their key is the inventory key, not an independently derived one. The current-evidence view is `unverified` throughout (no native reference exists).

## Independent derivation

Goal: obtain the expected answer for a claim from the artifact bytes and `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md` alone, never from score.py output or from the existing control's `expected`/`expected_positive`.

1. Open the original artifact `Core/ActorFramework/AF Specialty Messages.lvlib` (commit 371c631c, sha256 83bd1049...87d0, from the read-only environment copy).
2. Parse it as XML (stdlib `xml.etree`, or by eye). Read the `LVVersion` attribute of the root `<Library>`: the file text is `<Library LVVersion="20008000">`. Literal `20008000`; locator `/Library/@LVVersion`.
3. Count `<Property>` children of `<Library>` in document order: 1 NI.Lib.Icon, 2 NI.Lib.SourceVersion, 3 NI.Lib.Version, 4 NI.LV.All.SourceOnly. Literal at `/Library/Property[4]/@Name`: `NI.LV.All.SourceOnly`.
4. evaluation.md (tasks/oracle rows) requires an answer plus a source location in the original, and says the exporter's own output is not a reference. Structure checks without native evidence do not confirm LabVIEW behaviour. So the derived key is a literal-at-location fact only; it must not be stated as what LabVIEW resolves or displays.
5. Compare the derived literals with the inventory (`benchmark/cases/dev/library-specialty.json`) only afterwards, in the reviewer step. Any disagreement is reported, not reconciled by the deriver.

Independence caveat: the author of this plan saw the A0001/A0002 inventory values while measuring, so this session must not be the deriver.

## Proposed control

- Fixture: `benchmark/challenges/library-specialty.json` (3 controls today; one small artifact whose XML literals are checkable by eye).
- New case name (added by a later task, not now): `positive-control-independent-key`.
